family: A — missing tag guard on a READ
obligation: I4/O1 — must not read value.str.val / value.ht / value.obj from a zval whose type tag does not select that member
mechanism: A zval is a hand-rolled tagged union: a `zvalue_value` union (lval/dval/str{val,len}/ht/obj) plus a separate `zend_uchar type` field (Zend/zend.h:275-293). The Z_STRVAL_P / Z_ARRVAL_P family (Zend/zend_operators.h:234-275) expand directly to `(zval).value.str.val` and `(zval).value.ht` and consult nothing; Z_TYPE is a wholly separate macro that the payload accessors never invoke. At zend_exceptions.c:551 `zend_error_va(E_ERROR, Z_STRVAL_P(file), Z_LVAL_P(line), "Uncaught %s\n  thrown", Z_STRVAL_P(str))` reads the `file` and `string` properties as `char *` with no IS_STRING test, although a user subclass may assign any type to them. The attacker therefore chooses the pointer value outright.
harm_limb: both — reading `.str.val` out of a zval whose live member is `lval` yields an attacker-chosen `char *` and the printf-family consumer dereferences it (wild-pointer-deref). The same read on a benign-but-mistyped value (e.g. IS_DOUBLE) instead yields a defined-but-meaningless bit pattern that is merely printed, with no UB (silent-wrong-value). Which limb fires is decided by the tag the attacker plants, not by the code.
benign_behaviour: Given a well-formed tagged record whose tag says STRING, the kernel walks the pointed-to bytes to the declared length and folds them into the checksum; given LONG it folds the integer. A plausible u64 checksum is a running FNV-1a over (tag byte, then the tag-selected payload bytes) for every record in the blob — exactly reproducible by model.py, and equal to the C result on every benign input.
adversarial_trigger: A record whose tag byte says LONG but which a later opcode reads through the STRING accessor. Corpus ships reproducers: CRASH-036.php (`$this->file = 0x41414141;` inside an Exception subclass, then `throw`), CRASH-037.php (unserialize plants a non-array `trace`), CRASH-101.php.
self_containment: narrowed — needs the zval struct (16 bytes) and the accessor macros, nothing else. The property table can be modelled as a small fixed-slot array rather than a HashTable; the exception object and the class hierarchy are not needed to exhibit the defect.
blob_drivability: Directly. Blob = an opcode stream: `SET <slot> <tag> <8-byte payload>` builds a tagged value in a fixed slot array; `READ_AS_STR <slot>` folds the slot's `.str.val`/`.str.len` into the checksum; `READ_AS_LONG <slot>` folds `.lval`. Benign streams pair each SET with the matching READ; the adversarial stream pairs `SET t=LONG` with `READ_AS_STR`. p27 already decodes an opcode stream holding 32 raw pointers, so the shape is precedented.
hotness: none directly measurable — see NOTES.md: ASan reports no type-confusion class at all, so the 123-render census cannot speak to this axis. The *accessor macros* are however the single most-used construct in the engine (Z_* appears throughout every ext), so the read itself is maximally hot even though this particular call site is an error path.
mechanism_distinctness: The missing guard is on a READ, and there is NO guard of any kind at the site. This is the baseline against which B (a guard exists but tests the wrong tag), C (a helper launders the tag), D (the tag is inferred from the creation path) and E (a later WRITE invalidates a check that did hold) are all defined.
risks: Extracting only this row risks presenting the whole type axis as 'they forgot an if', which the other candidates show is false. Also: on a 64-bit build `str.val` (8B) fully overlays `lval` (8B), so `.str.len` reads bytes the lval write never touched — if the kernel zero-initialises its slots the uninitialised-read limb disappears and only the wild-pointer limb remains. Decide deliberately whether slots are zeroed.

family: B — guard present, but on the WRONG TAG (colliding IS_* namespaces)
c_lines: 1196-1197 (function zend_do_begin_method_call); tag namespaces at Zend/zend_compile.h:285-288 and Zend/zend.h:387-396; fault in Zend/zend_operators.c
invariant: I4 — tag matches payload (exemplar case for I4 in the blind labelling); also I3
mechanism: PHP has TWO unrelated `IS_*` enumerations whose values numerically collide. Zend/zend_compile.h:285-288 defines the *operand-kind* tag `IS_CONST=(1<<0)=1, IS_TMP_VAR=2, IS_VAR=4, IS_UNUSED=8` on a `znode`; Zend/zend.h:387-396 defines the *value-type* tag `IS_NULL=0, IS_LONG=1, IS_DOUBLE=2, IS_STRING=3, IS_ARRAY=4, IS_OBJECT=5` on a zval. Both headers are included everywhere. The `__clone` compile guard tests `last_op->op2.op_type == IS_CONST` — the operand-kind tag, which says only 'this operand is a literal' — and then immediately reads `last_op->op2.u.constant.value.str.len` and `.str.val` as though the *zval's own* `.type` had been checked for IS_STRING. It never is.
harm_limb: both, in a single expression, which is why this is the strongest row on the axis. `.str.val` overlays `lval`, so it hands the integer literal to zend_binary_strcasecmp as a `char *` (wild-pointer-deref, attacker-chosen address: `$v->{0x804a010}()`). `.str.len` reads union bytes that writing `lval` never wrote — stale parser-stack data (uninitialised read, silent). The blind labelling marks this case I4 **and I3** for exactly that reason. The uninit length is also what makes the guard *pass*: the leftover happened to be 7 == sizeof("__clone")-1.
benign_behaviour: For a literal operand whose value-tag really is STRING, the kernel compares the literal's bytes against a fixed keyword and folds a 1/0 match result plus the literal into the checksum. Checksum: FNV-1a over (operand-kind tag, value tag, keyword-match bit, payload) per instruction.
adversarial_trigger: A literal operand carrying operand-kind CONST but value-tag LONG. Corpus ships CRASH-144.php: `$abcdefg->{1}();` — one line, no classes, and the crash happens during COMPILATION before any output. The 7-character variable name is load-bearing: it is what leaves 7 in the stale length slot.
self_containment: narrowed — needs a two-field operand record (operand-kind tag + embedded tagged value) and one keyword comparison. No compiler, no symbol table, no objects. The 'stale stack data' can be reproduced with a scratch buffer the kernel reuses across instructions.
blob_drivability: Yes, and unusually cleanly. Blob = instruction stream where each instruction carries `op_kind` and, if op_kind==CONST, an inline tagged constant. The kernel's guard checks op_kind only, then folds `.str.len` bytes from `.str.val`. Benign streams emit CONST+STRING; the adversarial stream emits CONST+LONG. The stale-length effect falls out naturally if the decoder writes constants into a reused slot without clearing it.
hotness: Compile path — reached by every `include`, `eval`, lint pass or template compiler on untrusted PHP, i.e. anything that merely *parses*. Not measurable in the ASan census (compile-time, and no ASan class covers it).
mechanism_distinctness: A guard IS present on the READ and it PASSES; it simply interrogates a different tag field in a different namespace than the one that governs the union. This is categorically not 'a missing if' (family A) — it is a namespace collision between two enums that share a prefix and overlap in value. Nothing else in my set has this shape.
risks: The numeric collision (IS_CONST==1==IS_LONG, IS_VAR==4==IS_ARRAY) is what makes the confusion silent rather than obviously wrong. If the extraction gives the two tag enums disjoint value ranges, the defect becomes conspicuous and the row stops modelling the original. Preserve the collision deliberately, and say so in spec.md.

family: J — wrong PC stride on an early-exit path; a data word decoded as an instruction
c_lines: 1742-1749 (op_data set up, increment_opline=1), 1761-1770 (early exit via NEXT_OPCODE), 1792-1795 (correct exit via INC_OPCODE then NEXT_OPCODE), 1317-1320 (NEXT_OPCODE), 4427 (zend_opcode_handlers[ZEND_OP_DATA] = NULL)
obligation: control transfers only to a real instruction boundary
mechanism: Compound assignment to an array dimension is encoded as a TWO-word instruction: the opcode word plus a trailing `ZEND_OP_DATA` word that carries the extra operands (`zend_op *op_data = opline+1`, :1742). The handler sets `increment_opline = 1` at :1749 to record that it must advance the program counter by two. The normal exit honours that (`if (increment_opline) INC_OPCODE();` then `NEXT_OPCODE();`, :1792-1795). But the early-exit path taken when the fetched dimension yields `EG(error_zval_ptr)` jumps straight to `NEXT_OPCODE();` at :1769, which is just `EX(opline)++` (:1317-1320) — a stride of ONE. The executor then fetches the trailing data word as if it were an instruction and calls `zend_opcode_handlers[ZEND_OP_DATA]`, which is explicitly `NULL` (:4427).
harm_limb: wild-pointer-deref — specifically an indirect CALL through a NULL function pointer, which is a distinctly different consumer from the read-side derefs elsewhere on this axis. There is no silent limb: the data word's `opcode` field always selects the NULL slot.
benign_behaviour: The kernel decodes a variable-length instruction stream (1-word and 2-word forms), executing each and folding its result into the checksum, advancing the PC by the form's true width. On any benign stream it terminates having executed exactly the encoded instructions, and the checksum is the fold of their results.
adversarial_trigger: A 2-word instruction whose operand resolves to the error sentinel, so the handler takes the early exit. Corpus ships CRASH-023.php. In blob terms: any 2-word instruction followed by an early-exit condition the blob can set.
self_containment: verbatim-ish — this is the one candidate whose original C shape IS the pinned kernel shape. An instruction array, a PC, a dispatch table with a NULL entry, and a two-word form. No zvals strictly required (the error sentinel can be any flagged slot).
blob_drivability: Maximally. The blob IS the instruction stream; no adaptation needed. Include a handler table with a deliberately NULL entry for the data-word opcode, exactly as the original does. This is the most literal blob-to-C correspondence in my whole set.
hotness: Hot — the executor dispatch loop is the hottest loop in PHP. `zend_do_fcall_common_helper` / `execute` dominate the ASan stack census (11445 and 3199 frames respectively across 2534 logs), confirming the dispatch loop is on every real request.
mechanism_distinctness: Not a read guard, not a write, and not an ordering bug within a data structure: it is a CONTROL-FLOW stride error over a variable-length encoding. The 'type confusion' here is data-vs-code — a word that is operand payload gets decoded as an opcode. Unique in my set and the only one whose consumer is an indirect call.
risks: If the extracted kernel's dispatch table has no NULL entry (e.g. every opcode maps to a real handler), the trailing word decodes to *some* handler and the harm becomes a silent wrong checksum rather than a fault. That is still a valid limb, but it changes the row's headline — pin which one spec.md wants.

family: C — a helper LAUNDERS the tag; the caller draws a stronger conclusion than the helper licenses
c_lines: 2688-2695 (HASH_OF check then unconditional struct copy), 2728/2730 (confused Z_ARRVAL_P read); macro at Zend/zend_API.h:519; fault at Zend/zend_hash.c:460
mechanism: `HASH_OF(p)` (Zend/zend_API.h:519) is `((p)->type==IS_ARRAY ? (p)->value.ht : (((p)->type==IS_OBJECT ? Z_OBJ_HT_P(p)->get_properties(...) : NULL)))` — it returns a valid HashTable* for BOTH arrays and objects. array_unique uses it as its type check: `target_hash = HASH_OF(*array); if (!target_hash) { error }` (:2688-2692). An OBJECT passes. It then does the struct copy `*return_value = **array;` at :2695, which copies the zval WHOLE — payload *and* the IS_OBJECT tag. From :2728 onward the code reads `Z_ARRVAL_P(return_value)`, i.e. `.value.ht`, out of a zval still tagged IS_OBJECT whose live member is `.value.obj` (a `{zend_object_handle handle; zend_object_handlers *handlers;}`). The object handle is thus reinterpreted as a HashTable pointer and passed to zend_hash_del.
harm_limb: wild-pointer-deref — the object handle is a small integer (typically 1), so `ht` is a near-NULL pointer and `nIndex = h & ht->nTableMask` at zend_hash.c:460 faults. A silent limb is possible in principle if the handle ever aliased mapped memory, but not on this path.
benign_behaviour: Given an ARRAY-tagged container the kernel copies it, sorts a bucket index, and deletes duplicate entries, folding the surviving key/value pairs into the checksum. Deterministic and independently modellable.
adversarial_trigger: An OBJECT-tagged value passed where an array is expected — it must be one the laundering helper accepts. Corpus ships CRASH-079.php: `array_unique(new C)` with three properties, two duplicates.
self_containment: narrowed — needs the two-arm helper, the whole-zval struct copy, and a hash-ish container. The 'object' arm only has to return *some* valid table pointer for the benign case; the confusion comes from the tag surviving the copy, not from real object machinery.
blob_drivability: Yes. Blob opcodes: `MAKE_ARRAY <slot> <n entries>`, `MAKE_OBJECT <slot> <n props>`, `UNIQUE <src> <dst>`. The kernel's UNIQUE calls the laundering helper for its validity check, struct-copies the source zval into dst, then reads dst through the ARRAY accessor. A blob that emits MAKE_OBJECT then UNIQUE is the adversarial input.
hotness: array_unique is a common userland call; not separately visible in the ASan census (LTO-inlined, see NOTES.md).
mechanism_distinctness: The missing guard is on a READ, but unlike family A a check IS performed and passes — the defect is that the helper's postcondition ('this is array-or-object') is weaker than the conclusion the caller draws ('this is array'). The tag is then carried intact across a struct copy to a second variable, so the confusion happens at a different site than the check. Complementary to candidate #13, which misuses the SAME macro in the opposite direction.
risks: If the extraction makes the helper's object-arm return NULL (simpler to write), the row collapses into an ordinary null check and the mechanism is lost. The object arm MUST return a usable pointer for the benign case — that is the whole point.

family: F — statement ORDERING: a count field and its container are transiently inconsistent across a re-entrancy window
c_lines: 466-497 (unlink at 467-488, HANDLE_BLOCK_INTERRUPTIONS at 466, pDestructor at 489-491, nNumOfElements-- at 497 — outside the blocked window); consumer at ext/standard/array.c:1884-1894
invariant: I3 — initialised before read (exemplar case for I3 in the blind labelling); also I12
obligation: I3/O3 — a length/count field paired with an array must never exceed the number of slots actually written
mechanism: `zend_hash_del_key_or_index` fully unlinks the bucket from `arBuckets`, `pListHead`, `pListTail` and `pInternalPointer` at :467-488, then calls the element destructor at :489-491, and only decrements `ht->nNumOfElements` at :497. At PHP 5.0 the destructor can be arbitrary userland `__destruct`. So there is a window in which re-entrant code observes `nNumOfElements == (live buckets) + 1`. The author evidently knew the window mattered — the surgery is bracketed by `HANDLE_BLOCK_INTERRUPTIONS()` at :466 / `HANDLE_UNBLOCK_INTERRUPTIONS()` at :496 — but the decrement was placed one line OUTSIDE that bracket.
harm_limb: silent-wrong-value first, then wild-pointer-deref. A consumer that merely reports the count returns a number that is wrong by one with no UB at all. A consumer that uses the count as an emptiness test and then trusts a fallible accessor (candidate #11) escalates it to an uninitialised-pointer dereference.
benign_behaviour: The kernel maintains a keyed container with an element count; insert, delete and 'pop the last element' all keep the count in step, and the checksum folds each popped key/value plus the running count. Straight-line correct with no re-entrancy in the blob.
adversarial_trigger: A delete whose element destructor re-enters the same container. Corpus ships CRASH-153.php: a class whose `__destruct` calls `array_pop($GLOBALS['a'])`, then `unset($a[0])`.
self_containment: narrowed — needs a bucket list with a count field and a per-element destructor hook. NO userland, no objects: the destructor is just a function pointer stored on the container, and the blob decides which callback it points at.
blob_drivability: Yes, and the re-entrancy is easy to express. Blob opcodes: `INS <key> <val>`, `DEL <key>`, `SET_DTOR <callback-id>`. Callback id 0 = no-op (benign); callback id 1 = 're-enter and pop'. The adversarial blob is INS, SET_DTOR 1, DEL. Re-entrancy depth is bounded by a counter so the kernel always terminates.
hotness: zend_hash_del_key_or_index is core to every array write in PHP. Not separately visible in the ASan census — see NOTES.md: zero `zend_hash_*` frames appear in 2534 logs because the census build is max-LTO and inlines them.
mechanism_distinctness: This is the ORDERING mechanism, the third category the brief asked me to separate. No guard is missing and no tag is misread; two writes that must be simultaneous are merely sequenced, and a callback runs between them. Distinct from every read-side and write-side candidate.
risks: If the extracted kernel's re-entrant path happens not to observe the count (e.g. it iterates the list directly), the window exists but is unobservable and the row measures nothing. The consumer must gate on the COUNT, not on the list — that is the coupling that makes the ordering matter.

family: I — the guard is applied at the wrong POINTER DEPTH
obligation: every dereferenced pointer is non-null at the depth actually dereferenced
mechanism: `value` is a `zval **`. The iterator's `get_current_data(iter, &value)` at :3831 sets `value` to point AT the iterator's internal `zval *` slot, so `value` is unconditionally non-NULL. The guard at :3832 is `if (!value)` — depth 1 — and can therefore never fire. The property that actually matters is at depth 2: when the userland `current()` throws, the iterator's internal slot is left holding NULL, so `*value == NULL` while `value != NULL`. At :3853 `(*value)->refcount++` dereferences it. The correct guard is `if (!*value)`; the fault address is NULL + offsetof(zval, refcount) = 0x10.
harm_limb: wild-pointer-deref (a NULL deref at a small fixed offset). No silent limb: the read is a refcount increment, so it is a write to NULL+0x10 and always faults.
benign_behaviour: The kernel iterates a source, asking a callback to hand back a pointer-to-slot each step, and folds each yielded element into the checksum. On any stream where the callback always fills its slot, it is straightforwardly correct.
adversarial_trigger: A callback that returns success but leaves its out-slot NULL — i.e. an error path that reports through a side channel rather than the return value. Corpus ships CRASH-143.php: an Iterator whose `current()` throws on the third element.
self_containment: narrowed — needs only a two-level pointer out-parameter and a callback that can fail. No iterators, no exceptions: the 'throw' is just the callback setting a flag and leaving the slot NULL.
blob_drivability: Yes. Blob = `<n elements>` followed by per-element `<mode>` bytes; mode 0 = fill the slot normally, mode 1 = leave it NULL. The kernel loops, calls the fill callback, applies the depth-1 guard, then dereferences at depth 2. A blob with any mode-1 byte is adversarial.
hotness: The foreach fetch is per-iteration of every object loop; upstream rewrote this exact block for performance (commit fc96c7f7fa18 removes the per-iteration temporary array), which is independent evidence it was hot enough to optimise.
mechanism_distinctness: The guard is on a READ and it is PRESENT and CORRECTLY WRITTEN — for a different type. It checks `zval*` when the value at risk is `zval**`. Distinct from family A (no guard), B (wrong tag namespace) and C (helper laundering): here the tag is irrelevant; the confusion is about how many stars deep the invariant lives.
risks: In a kernel where the out-parameter is an index rather than a pointer, the two depths collapse and the bug becomes unwritable. Keep the double indirection literal.

family: E — type-changing WRITE through an unseparated shared value; a check that DID hold is invalidated later
c_lines: 1935-1949 (type checks then in-place conversions), 2077 (harmful in-place convert_to_long_ex on an aliased element), 2116-2126 (fault: memcpy bounded by a now-stale length); caller-side twin at Zend/zend_execute_API.c:730-753; macros at Zend/zend_operators.h:210-214 and Zend/zend.h:554-571
obligation: I4/O2 — a type established by an earlier check or conversion must still hold at the point of use, including across any operation that can run user code
mechanism: `convert_to_long_ex` and friends expand to `convert_to_ex_master` (zend_operators.h:210-214): `if ((*ppzv)->type != IS_LONG) { SEPARATE_ZVAL_IF_NOT_REF(ppzv); convert_to_long(*ppzv); }`. `SEPARATE_ZVAL_IF_NOT_REF` (zend.h:568-571) is `if (!PZVAL_IS_REF(*ppzv)) SEPARATE_ZVAL(ppzv);` — i.e. it is a NO-OP precisely when `is_ref == 1`. So a conversion that was written to be copy-on-write silently becomes an IN-PLACE RETYPE whenever the value is a reference. substr_replace checks each argument's type at :1935-1949 and then, at :2077, converts an element in place; when the same zval is reachable through two argument names the type conclusion drawn at :1941 is retroactively false, and the length `f` cached from the pre-conversion string is used to bound the memcpy at :2116-2126. zend_execute_API.c:730-753 is the same defect one frame up: when a parameter is a reference but the callee does not declare it by-reference, the else-branch at :751-753 merely bumps the refcount and hands the shared, `is_ref` zval to the internal function, where the very same no-op separation applies.
harm_limb: both. The retype alone is a silent-wrong-value (the caller's variable changes type behind its back, no UB). The escalation is a wild/out-of-bounds pointer use: a length cached before the retype bounds a memcpy over a buffer the retype shortened or replaced.
benign_behaviour: The kernel normalises each argument to a required type, then splices bytes using a length derived from the normalised value, folding the result into the checksum. On unaliased inputs it is a plain, correct splice.
adversarial_trigger: Two argument slots aliased to one storage cell, with the alias flagged 'shared'. Corpus ships CRASH-104.php and CRASH-058.php.
self_containment: narrowed — needs a value cell with a share flag, a conversion helper that skips copying when the flag is set, and a caller that caches a length across the conversion. No refcounting GC required; a boolean `shared` bit suffices.
blob_drivability: Yes. Blob opcodes: `NEW <slot> <tag> <payload>`, `ALIAS <slotA> <slotB>` (points both names at one cell and sets shared=1), `SPLICE <str> <from> <len>`. Benign blobs never ALIAS; the adversarial blob aliases the `len` and `str` slots before SPLICE.
hotness: convert_to_*_ex is on the argument-normalisation path of essentially every internal function call. Not separately visible in the census (LTO-inlined).
mechanism_distinctness: The missing guard is on a WRITE, not a read — this is the axis's second limb and the manager's hypothesised 'second mechanism'. Confirmed distinct, and stronger than hypothesised: the two rows share a single named root cause (the is_ref no-op in SEPARATE_ZVAL_IF_NOT_REF), seen from the callee side (104) and the caller side (058). Note these are CWE-843 rows, i.e. the second mechanism lives INSIDE the eleven, not outside them.
risks: Easy to extract in a way that shows only the silent retype and never the memcpy escalation; the cached-length-across-conversion step is the load-bearing part and is easy to drop by accident. Also, if the kernel separates unconditionally the row becomes a no-op — the share flag must genuinely suppress the copy.

family: A2 — PRESENCE checked, TYPE not; plus a null-check that cannot help
c_lines: 640-651 (four unguarded Z_STRVAL_PP after successful lookups); wild deref at ext/standard/info.c:828
obligation: I4/O3 — a value handed to a consumer that reads it at a fixed C type must be converted or rejected before that consumer reads it
mechanism: Four consecutive blocks at :640-651 do `if (zend_hash_find(&EG(symbol_table), "PHP_SELF", ..., &data) != FAILURE) php_info_print_table_row(2, "PHP_SELF", Z_STRVAL_PP(data));`. The lookup establishes that the KEY EXISTS; the code then treats that as licence to read the VALUE as a `char *`. The symbol table is the global variable table, so a script writes `$PHP_SELF = 1;` and the accessor returns `.value.str.val` from an IS_LONG zval. The consumer at :828 is `if (!row_element || !*row_element)` — a null check IS present, and it is useless: the confused pointer is a non-null small integer, so the guard passes and `*row_element` faults.
harm_limb: wild-pointer-deref, with a notable twist: the defensive null check at the consumer is present and passes. If the planted integer is 0 the guard fires and the output is merely wrong (silent limb), so the attacker chooses the limb by choosing the integer.
benign_behaviour: The kernel looks up a set of fixed keys in a table, and for each hit folds the key plus the string value's bytes into the checksum, skipping misses. Correct and total on well-typed tables.
adversarial_trigger: A table entry present under an expected key but carrying a non-string tag. Corpus ships CRASH-093.php — two lines: `$PHP_SELF = 1; phpinfo(INFO_VARIABLES);`.
self_containment: narrowed — a small keyed table of tagged values plus a consumer that null-checks then dereferences. No SAPI, no output layer.
blob_drivability: Yes. Blob = a sequence of `PUT <key-id> <tag> <payload>` records followed by an implicit 'report' phase over a fixed key list. The kernel's report step folds `Z_STRVAL`-style bytes for every key it finds, applying only the null check.
hotness: none — phpinfo is not a hot path. Its value is the mechanism, not the frequency.
mechanism_distinctness: Missing guard on a READ, but the distinguishing feature is that a DIFFERENT, weaker check succeeded first (key presence) and a second, irrelevant check (nullness) also succeeded at the consumer. Family A's baseline row has no check at all. This row is about guards that exist and do not constrain the property at risk.
risks: Near-duplicate of candidate #1 at the accessor level; its distinctness rests entirely on the presence-check and the useless null-check being preserved. If the extraction drops the null check at the consumer, this row becomes candidate #1 and should be merged.

family: A3 — the CONTAINER's type is checked; its ELEMENTS' are not
c_lines: 293 (`HashTable *ht = Z_ARRVAL_PP(frame);` on an unchecked element), 304 (zend_hash_find on the wild ht), 310-311 (a SECOND unguarded read: Z_STRLEN_PP/Z_STRVAL_PP on the looked-up `file`); fault at Zend/zend_hash.c:850
mechanism: `_build_trace_string` is applied to each element of the exception's `trace` array. Its very first statement, :293, is `HashTable *ht = Z_ARRVAL_PP(frame);` — it assumes every element is itself an array. A malformed frame (a NULL or a long) makes `ht` a wild pointer, and :304 `zend_hash_find(ht, "file", ...)` reads `ht->nTableMask` at zend_hash.c:850. The same function then commits the error a second time at :310-311: having found `file` by key, it reads `Z_STRLEN_PP(file)` and `Z_STRVAL_PP(file)` without checking that element's tag either. So one function contains both the element-level and the presence-not-type variants.
harm_limb: wild-pointer-deref at :304. The :310-311 read adds a second, independent wild-pointer limb through a different accessor.
benign_behaviour: The kernel walks a container of sub-containers, looks up two fixed keys in each, and folds the found values into the checksum, producing a rendered-string-length-like total. Correct on well-formed nested input.
adversarial_trigger: A container whose elements are not all sub-containers. Corpus ships CRASH-039.php, which plants the malformed frame via `unserialize()` of a crafted private-property payload.
self_containment: narrowed — a nested container and a per-element callback. Serialisation is NOT needed: the blob plants the malformed element directly, which is strictly simpler than the PHP reproducer.
blob_drivability: Yes, and more directly than in PHP. Blob = `<n frames>` then per frame `<tag> <payload-or-subtable>`. The kernel applies the callback to each frame, reading `.ht` unconditionally. Any frame with a non-table tag is adversarial.
hotness: none — exception rendering. Mechanism value only.
mechanism_distinctness: Missing guard on a READ, distinguished from #1 by WHERE the guard is missing: the top-level value's type was established (it is the `trace` property, and candidate #1's CRASH-037 covers the case where THAT is wrong), while the per-element type is assumed. Container-checked/element-unchecked is a distinct locus and generalises to every 'apply over a collection' API.
risks: Overlaps candidate #1 (same file, same accessor) and candidate #8 (the :310 read is a presence-not-type read). Genuinely a near-duplicate cluster — flagged as such for the manager. Its independent contribution is the container/element split.

family: H — an uninitialised struct is consumed as FUNCTION POINTERS because an attacker-controlled flag enables a path that reads fields the caller never wrote
c_lines: 369 (`glob_t globbuf;` uninitialised), 373 (user-supplied `long flags`), 394 (only gl_offs is set), 395 (glob() called with flags & GLOB_FLAGMASK); GLOB_FLAGMASK at :164 is `(~0)`
obligation: I3/O2 — must not use a value read from such a slot as a pointer, handle, size, or length
mechanism: `glob_t globbuf;` is a bare automatic at :369 — no initialiser, no memset. Only `globbuf.gl_offs = 0;` is written, at :394. The `flags` argument is an unvalidated user `long` (:368, :373) and the mask it passes through, `GLOB_FLAGMASK`, is `(~0)` on the branch taken here (:164) — it masks NOTHING. Setting the `GLOB_ALTDIRFUNC` bit therefore tells the C library to call `globbuf.gl_readdir`, `gl_opendir`, `gl_closedir`, `gl_stat`, `gl_lstat` — struct fields the caller never wrote. The callee makes indirect calls through uninitialised stack memory.
harm_limb: wild-pointer-deref via an indirect CALL through uninitialised stack. Silent limb possible if the leftover stack bytes happen to be zero (then the callee may take a null-check path), which makes the outcome build- and stack-history-dependent — itself a reportable property.
benign_behaviour: The kernel takes a pattern and a flags word, matches the pattern against a fixed in-blob name table using only the flag bits it understands, and folds the matching names into the checksum. Correct and deterministic for every flag value in the understood set.
adversarial_trigger: A flags word with a bit set that the kernel forwards but never validates, and which selects a callback-driven path. Corpus ships CRASH-087.php — literally `glob("*", 512);`.
self_containment: modelled — the real defect needs libc's glob(). The extraction must supply its own 'callee' that honours an ALTDIRFUNC-like bit by calling through caller-supplied function pointers. That is faithful to the mechanism (uninit fields consumed as callbacks) but is a re-implementation, not a lift.
blob_drivability: Yes. Blob = `<flags u32> <pattern> <name table>`. The kernel declares its options struct uninitialised, writes one field, ORs in the blob's flags with a mask that is all-ones, and calls the matcher, which calls through the callback fields when the bit is set.
mechanism_distinctness: Purely an INITIALISATION defect — no tag is misread and no guard is missing on any read the kernel itself performs. The read happens in the CALLEE, licensed by a flag the caller forwarded unvalidated. Unique in my set: the only candidate where the confused consumer is code the kernel does not own, and the only one whose 'guard' is a mask constant that was defined to be a no-op.
risks: The `(~0)` mask is the crux and is easy to lose: an extraction that masks the flags properly kills the bug outright. Also, whether the uninit bytes are nonzero depends on stack history, so the row may need a deliberate stack-priming step to be reproducible — note that in spec.md rather than discovering it during measurement.

family: G — a fallible call's out-parameter is left unwritten and its status is discarded
c_lines: 1884 (emptiness gated on the count), 1893 (`zend_hash_get_current_data(..., (void **)&val);` return value discarded), 1894 (`*return_value = **val;` on the never-assigned automatic)
obligation: I3/O1 — must not read a slot that has been allocated or declared but never assigned
mechanism: `_phpi_pop` gates on `zend_hash_num_elements(...) == 0` at :1884, positions the internal pointer, then calls `zend_hash_get_current_data(Z_ARRVAL_PP(stack), (void **)&val)` at :1893 WITHOUT storing or testing its SUCCESS/FAILURE result. When the container is really empty the callee returns FAILURE and never writes the out-parameter, leaving the automatic `zval **val` holding whatever the stack held. Line 1894 then dereferences it twice: `*return_value = **val;`. The C-side defect is complete on its own — it needs the stale count only to REACH the failing call, and any other way of reaching it works equally well.
harm_limb: both, and this is the candidate where the silent limb is most interesting. If the leftover stack bytes form a readable address, the engine copies a FABRICATED zval — tag byte and union together — out to the caller, so an uninitialised read manufactures a well-formed-looking tagged value. That is an uninit-read feeding a type confusion. Where the bytes are unreadable it is an ordinary SEGV.
benign_behaviour: The kernel pops the last element of a container and folds it into the checksum, returning a sentinel when empty. Correct whenever the emptiness test and the accessor agree.
adversarial_trigger: Any path that makes the emptiness test and the accessor disagree. In the blob this need not involve re-entrancy at all — a `POP` opcode issued when the count field has been desynchronised is enough.
self_containment: verbatim — a container, a count, an out-parameter accessor returning a status, and a caller that ignores it. Nothing else.
blob_drivability: Yes, and this is the simplest kernel in my set. Blob = `INS`/`POP`/`DESYNC` opcodes; `DESYNC` bumps the count without inserting. The uninitialised local is real C: declare `T *val;` with no initialiser and let the failing accessor skip it.
hotness: array_pop/array_shift are common; not separately visible in the census (LTO-inlined).
mechanism_distinctness: Neither a read guard, a write, nor an ordering: it is a DISCARDED STATUS CODE producing an uninitialised local. Deliberately split from candidate #5 even though the corpus merges them into CRASH-153, because the two links are independently extractable and the blind labelling itself separates them (I3/O3 for the ordering, I3/O1+O2 for this). Manager may prefer to merge; I recommend not, because #5 needs a re-entrancy window and this one does not.
risks: A compiler may warn on the obviously-uninitialised local (-Wmaybe-uninitialized), and at -O2 may exploit the UB to do something unrelated to the C-level story. That is a genuine measurement hazard for a two-optimisation-level benchmark and should be checked early, not late.

family: D — an entry's type is inferred from HOW ONE PATH CREATES IT, while another path creates it differently
c_lines: 2970-2978 (find-or-create: the create arm calls array_init at :2973, the found arm is bare `hash = *find_hash;` at :2977), 2996 (add_next_index_zval(hash, element) — Z_ARRVAL_P on a possibly-scalar zval)
mechanism: The POP_ENTRY case implements find-or-create. If the key is absent it allocates and calls `array_init(hash)` (:2971-2975), so the created entry is certainly an array. If the key is present it simply takes `hash = *find_hash;` (:2977) and asks no questions. The author's warrant for treating `hash` as an array is 'the only code that creates entries here calls array_init' — but a DIFFERENT callback case (ZEND_INI_PARSER_ENTRY, for a plain `foo = 1`) has already inserted a STRING zval under the same key. At :2996 `add_next_index_zval(hash, element)` does `Z_ARRVAL_P(hash)`, reinterpreting the string's `char *` as a `HashTable *`.
harm_limb: wild-pointer-deref — the string payload is a real heap pointer, so the confused HashTable* points at readable heap and the code writes bucket structure over string bytes. This is the one candidate whose confusion lands on VALID mapped memory, so it corrupts rather than faults, and may not crash promptly.
benign_behaviour: The kernel parses a key/value record stream into a nested table, appending to a per-key list, and folds the resulting structure into the checksum. Correct whenever each key is used consistently as scalar or as list.
adversarial_trigger: A record stream that declares a key as a scalar and then appends to it as a list. Corpus ships CRASH-085.php, which writes an ini file containing `foo = 1` then `foo[] = 1`.
self_containment: narrowed — a keyed table, two insertion paths, and an append that assumes list-ness. The ini parser is not needed; the blob is the record stream.
blob_drivability: Yes, very naturally. Blob = records `SET <key> <scalar>` and `APPEND <key> <scalar>`. The kernel's APPEND does find-or-create and then appends without re-checking. `SET foo, APPEND foo` is the adversarial blob.
mechanism_distinctness: Missing guard on a READ, but the *reason* it is missing is a whole-program argument about creation paths rather than a local oversight: the invariant is 'entries under this key are arrays', which one code path establishes and another silently violates. Distinct from #4 (a helper launders the tag at the check site) and #1 (no argument was made at all). Closest to a genuine design-level defect.
risks: Because the confusion lands on valid heap the row may show corruption without a crash, so a naive 'does it segfault' oracle will call it clean. The checksum comparison against model.py is the real detector here — say so in spec.md.

family: C2 — the SAME laundering helper, misused in the opposite direction
c_lines: 612-613 (HASH_OF(stream->wrapperdata) passed straight to the hash walkers with no NULL test), 616/621/629 (Z_STRVAL_PP on unchecked elements); macro at Zend/zend_API.h:519
mechanism: `HASH_OF` returns NULL for anything that is neither array nor object. get_headers hands its result directly to `zend_hash_internal_pointer_reset_ex(HASH_OF(stream->wrapperdata), &pos)` at :612 and `zend_hash_get_current_data_ex(HASH_OF(...), ...)` at :613 with no NULL test, so a wrapperdata that is unset or scalar produces a NULL table walk. It then compounds the error at :616 and :621 by reading each element with `Z_STRVAL_PP(hdr)` and passing it to `strchr` without checking the element's tag.
harm_limb: wild-pointer-deref (NULL table walk at :612, then wild char* at :616/:621). No silent limb.
benign_behaviour: The kernel walks a table of string records, splits each at a delimiter, and folds the key/value halves into the checksum.
adversarial_trigger: A source whose table field is absent or mistyped. Corpus ships CRASH-111.php; corpus confidence for this row is `medium`, the lowest on my axis — flagged.
self_containment: narrowed — the laundering helper plus a table walk. No streams or wrappers needed.
blob_drivability: Yes, but it is the least interesting blob in the set: `<tag> <table-or-scalar>` then walk. Its value is the PAIRING with candidate #4 rather than its own kernel.
mechanism_distinctness: Same helper as #4, opposite error: #4 checks the helper's result for NULL and then over-concludes IS_ARRAY; #13 does not check it at all. Together they show that a two-arm accessor has two distinct ways of being misused, which is a better story than either alone. Recommend the manager treat #4 and #13 as one row with two limbs unless breadth is short.
risks: Weakest row on its own; corpus confidence is `medium` and the wrapperdata-is-NULL path may be reachable only in configurations the extraction will not model. Its justification is comparative.

family: K — a tag computed by ARITHMETIC on an enum, with the validity guard replicated on some arms and forgotten on one
c_lines: 751-775 (the switch: guarded arms at 752-757 and 770-775, unguarded arm at 763-765)
obligation: an emitted instruction's opcode and operand kinds form a combination the executor implements
mechanism: Opcode families are laid out at fixed strides, and the compiler selects a variant by ARITHMETIC on the opcode value: `opline->opcode -= 3` for read, `+= 3` for read-write, `+= 6` for isset, `+= 9` for func-arg, `+= 12` for unset (:756, :761, :764, :767, :774). Two arms guard against the illegal append-with-no-index form first — BP_VAR_R rejects `ZEND_FETCH_DIM_W` with `op2.op_type == IS_UNUSED` at :753-755, and BP_VAR_UNSET repeats the same test at :771-773. The BP_VAR_IS arm at :763-765 does the arithmetic with NO such guard, so `isset($a[])` emits a FETCH_DIM_IS whose op2 is UNUSED — an opcode/operand combination the executor never expects, driving the append (write) path under a read handler.
harm_limb: wild-pointer-deref (NULL). Silent limb unlikely: the executor's read handler has no branch for an unused index.
benign_behaviour: The kernel compiles a token stream into instructions by selecting an opcode variant per access mode, then executes them, folding results into the checksum. Correct for every mode/operand combination the guard set actually covers.
adversarial_trigger: The append form under the one access mode whose arm forgot the guard. Corpus ships CRASH-041.php.
self_containment: narrowed — a mode enum, a base-opcode table, stride arithmetic, per-arm guards, and a tiny executor with a table that has no handler for the illegal combination.
blob_drivability: Yes. Blob = `<mode> <base-op> <has-index> [index]` records. The kernel runs the guard-and-arithmetic step then executes. A record with mode=IS and has-index=0 is adversarial.
hotness: Compile path, same surface as candidate #2 (any include/eval/lint of untrusted source).
mechanism_distinctness: Neither a read guard nor a write nor an ordering: it is a guard-REPLICATION defect over a switch, combined with tag arithmetic. Two of five arms carry the check; one that needs it does not. Distinct from #3, which is also opcode-related but is a control-flow stride error at RUN time rather than a malformed emission at COMPILE time. The pair #3/#14 covers both halves of 'the instruction stream itself is the confused value'.
risks: The stride layout (+0/+3/+6/+9/+12) must be preserved or the arithmetic becomes arbitrary and the row loses its point. Also easy to accidentally make the illegal combination trap in the decoder, which would fix the bug.

family: L — an unconstructed caller-supplied slot is destructed/read on an early-exit path
c_lines: 242-247 (`if (EG(exception)) { zval_dtor(expr_copy); ... }` before expr_copy is ever constructed); caller's stack zval at Zend/zend_operators.c:1148
mechanism: `zend_make_printable_zval` receives `expr_copy`, an UNINITIALISED zval that the caller declared on its own stack (zend_operators.c:1148) for the callee to fill in. On the IS_OBJECT arm, if a user `__toString` handler left a pending exception, the function takes the early exit at :242-247 and calls `zval_dtor(expr_copy)` — destructing a slot it has not yet constructed. zval_dtor switches on the uninitialised `type` byte and frees the uninitialised union accordingly.
harm_limb: both — the blind labelling classes this one `uninit-read-silent`, so the headline is a silent wrong value (the leftover tag usually selects a no-op destructor arm and the caller then reads a fabricated string). Where the leftover tag selects a pointer-freeing arm it becomes a free of an uninitialised pointer. It is the axis's clearest 'reads an uninitialised TAG and dispatches on it' case.
benign_behaviour: The kernel renders a tagged value into a caller-provided output slot, folding the rendered bytes into the checksum. Correct on every path that constructs the slot before returning.
adversarial_trigger: A value whose user-supplied rendering hook signals failure, driving the early exit before construction. No crash reproducer — the corpus ships LOGIC-007.php under input/logic/, and the row is explicitly a non-crash class.
self_containment: narrowed — a caller-declared output slot, a callee that may exit early, and a tag-dispatched teardown. No exceptions needed; a failure flag suffices.
blob_drivability: Yes. Blob = `<tag> <payload> <hook-result>` records; hook-result=fail drives the early exit. The kernel declares the output slot uninitialised in the caller frame exactly as the original does.
hotness: String conversion of objects — common, not hot in the dispatch sense.
mechanism_distinctness: Distinct from #10 (uninit consumed as a function pointer in a CALLEE) and #11 (uninit local from a discarded status): here the uninitialised thing is a TAG, and the harm is that a switch dispatches on it. That makes it the direct bridge between the I3 and I4 halves of my axis, and the only candidate that is primarily a silent-wrong-value row.
risks: Non-crash class: `crashes_pristine_5_0_0` is n/a, so the 'exhibits the target error' half of the admission bar must be shown by checksum divergence rather than by a fault. That is a legitimate demonstration but needs stating up front. Also the leftover tag byte is stack-history-dependent, so reproducibility needs stack priming.
